transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I came in because my husband made me. Him and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy, but I'm not. I know for a fact they have been watching my moves on the floor and changing the pallet counts just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. They think I don't notice the numbers changing, but I do. 

Just like I noticed when they switched the shrink wrap on us. We used to use this blue-tinted wrap, which stretches way better, especially around the heavy stuff. I was moving these huge 40-pound bags of dog food yesterday... Purina, I think. My dog, Buster, he won't even touch Purina. He only likes the wet food in the little cans. My husband bought the wrong ones last week, the chicken flavor, and Buster threw it up all over the hallway rug. It's a really nice rug, too, I got it at a yard sale for like ten bucks, but I had to scrub it with baking soda for an hour just to get the smell out. Anyway, what were you asking?
How long have you believed that your coworkers have been watching you and changing the pallet counts to prevent you from getting the supervisor position?

I'd say... it's been about eight months now. The voices, and that feeling that people are watching me or changing my numbers and things... yeah, about eight months. It started right around when they brought in the new scanning guns for the inventory. They're these heavy black scanners, Motorola I think. 

My uncle had a Motorola flip phone back in the day, the Razr? Man, he loved that phone. He dropped it in a lake when we went fishing up at Lake George. We didn't even catch anything that day, just some tiny little sunfish that we had to throw back. Have you ever been fishing? You have to use the right bait, otherwise the fish just steal the worm right off the hook and you're just sitting there staring at the water for hours. It gets so boring. But yeah, eight months.
You mentioned hearing voices—what do these voices say to you, and do they ever tell you to do things?

Well, it's usually just this one guy's voice. Like, sometimes when I'm in the aisle at the warehouse, or even just at home folding clothes, I'll hear him clear as day. He just says, "Nicole, check it again." And I look around, and nobody is even near me. It's so weird when I'm folding clothes, too, because I'm really particular about how the towels get folded. My husband just kind of rolls them up and shoves them in the linen closet, and it drives me crazy. You can't fit as many in there if you don't fold them flat, you know? We have this really tiny closet in the hallway, the door always sticks on the carpet because the hinges are loose. I told him to fix the hinges like three weeks ago, but he's always watching those car restoration shows on TV. He thinks he's going to buy an old Mustang and fix it up, but we don't even have a garage. Where's he gonna put a Mustang? In the driveway? The HOA would throw a fit. They already sent us a letter about the trash cans being out too long. But no, the voice doesn't tell me to do bad things or anything, just tells me to check things.

You mentioned the symptoms started about eight months ago when the new scanning guns came in. Before that time, did you have any major stressful events happening in your life—like problems at home, with your husband, or anything else that was really upsetting?

Well, I guess... actually, the arguments with my husband started getting really bad before that. Probably about ten months ago? Yeah, it was ten months ago, right when I first started talking about trying for that shift-supervisor role. He didn't think I should go for it because of the hours. 

He hates when I work the late shift because he says he can't sleep when I'm not in the bed. But he sleeps just fine on the couch when he falls asleep watching TV! He fell asleep during the Super Bowl last year, right in the middle of the halftime show. I don't even know how you sleep through all those flashing lights and the music. We had made all these snacks, too. I made those little cocktail wieners in the crockpot with the barbecue sauce and grape jelly. Have you ever tried that? It sounds gross, the jelly part, but it actually makes this really good sweet and sour glaze. I got the recipe from my aunt Linda. She used to bring them to every family reunion, but then she moved to Florida. Tampa, I think. Or maybe Clearwater. One of those places with the really bad humidity. My hair gets so frizzy in the humidity, I can't stand it. But yeah, ten months ago is when the arguments got bad.
Do you think there's any possibility that the coworkers might not actually be watching you or changing the pallet counts—that maybe this could all be in your head?

No, I know I'm not making it up. That's actually why I'm here, I came in because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy or something. But I know for a fact they have been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. They think I don't notice, but I do. Just like I notice when the milk is left out. My husband did that yesterday, just left the gallon of 2% sitting right on the counter for hours. It gets warm so fast, and then it smells weird when you put it in cereal. I eat Cheerios every morning, the Honey Nut kind. The regular ones taste like cardboard, don't you think? My grandma used to make us eat the regular ones when we'd stay over at her house in the summer. She'd put sliced bananas in it to make it better, but the bananas would get all mushy in the milk. I hate mushy fruit. It's a texture thing, I think. But no, I'm not crazy, they're definitely messing with my numbers.
Besides the coworkers watching you and changing the pallet counts at work, do you believe other people or things are also plotting against you or trying to harm you in other areas of your life?

No, not like strangers or the government or anything weird like that. Just... well, exactly what I was just saying a second ago. It's my husband and the warehouse guys. They're the ones acting like I'm the crazy one, teaming up to watch me and mess with my pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. I know they're doing it. 

And that supervisor job pays an extra three dollars an hour, you know. Three dollars! That really adds up on a biweekly check. I was telling my sister I wanted to use the extra money to finally get a new mattress, because ours has this huge dip right in the middle on my side. It's just an old spring mattress. My sister told me to get one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a cardboard box. Have you seen those commercials? They just cut the plastic and it puffs up into a whole bed right in your room. It's wild. But she said hers smelled like weird chemicals for like two weeks after she opened it. I definitely couldn't deal with that. I have a really sensitive nose. Like, I can tell when the forklift drivers at work have been smoking on their breaks before they even get back inside the building. The smell just clings to their safety vests. The neon yellow ones, you know? They get so dirty anyway, I don't know why they don't make them in a darker color. Neon yellow just shows every single smudge of grease.
When you hear this man's voice telling you to 'check it again,' do you know who this person is, or do you have any idea why he's specifically talking to you?

I don't know who he is. It's just... it's just this man's voice, clear as day. I'll be in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes, and he'll say, "Nicole, check it again." And there's nobody anywhere near me. It's so weird when I'm folding clothes, especially the towels. I have to fold them in thirds, you know? If you just fold them in half, they don't stack right in the linen closet. My husband always just rolls them up in a ball and shoves them on the shelf, and it drives me crazy. The whole stack falls over when you try to pull one out. We have these really nice dark blue ones we got for our wedding, but the color is starting to fade from washing them so much. I think our water is too hard. It leaves those white crusty spots on the showerhead, too. Have you ever tried soaking a showerhead in a bag of vinegar? My neighbor told me to do that, you just tie a plastic bag full of white vinegar around it with a rubber band and leave it overnight. It really works, but then the whole bathroom smells like a pickle jar for two days. I can't stand the smell of pickles. Especially the sweet ones. Dill is okay on a burger, I guess, but sweet pickles are just wrong. Who wants a sweet cucumber? But yeah, I don't know who the guy is, he just tells me to check it again.

When you say the coworkers are changing the pallet counts and watching you—do you think they're doing this in ways that would be physically possible for them to do, or do you think they might be using special equipment, technology, or some kind of special powers to watch you or change the numbers?

No, no special powers or anything crazy like that. Like I said, I came in here because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm the crazy one, but I know for a fact they've been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. They just go into the system and change the numbers when I'm not looking, or they physically move the pallets. It's just regular stuff, but they're doing it to mess with me. 

They use those handheld scanners, the ones with the little laser barcode readers. You have to make sure you hear the beep when you scan it, otherwise it didn't register. Sometimes the barcode stickers get all wrinkled or torn, and then you have to type the whole SKU number in by hand. It takes forever. And the buttons on those scanners are so tiny, if you have gloves on, you always hit two buttons at once. I bought these special gloves on Amazon that have the touchscreen tips on the fingers, but they didn't even work. They were supposed to be thermal, too, because the warehouse gets freezing in the winter. Especially over by the loading docks when the bay doors are open. The wind just whips right through there. I started wearing two pairs of socks, but then my work boots feel too tight and my toes get numb. My husband said I should just buy bigger boots, but they're expensive. Good steel-toe boots are like a hundred and fifty bucks. You can't just buy the cheap ones at Walmart, they fall apart in a month and the steel toe part always digs into the top of your foot when you walk. I had a pair once that gave me a blister the size of a quarter on my heel. I had to put those squishy gel band-aids on it for weeks. But yeah, they're just using the regular scanners to change my counts. Nothing high-tech.

When your coworkers watch you and change the pallet counts—do you think what they're doing is something that people could actually do in the normal way, or does it seem impossible or strange in a way that doesn't make sense even though you know it's happening?

I mean, like I just told you, it's totally normal stuff they're doing. I feel like I'm repeating myself, but I only came in here because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. But I know for a fact they have been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. It's not impossible or magic, it's just them being sneaky behind my back. 

And honestly, I really want that supervisor spot mostly because they get to use the front office breakroom. Have you seen the office breakroom? They have one of those fancy Keurig machines in there, not just the gross drip coffee we have out on the warehouse floor. That floor coffee tastes like burnt dirt, I swear they never wash the glass pot. It always has that brown ring baked into the bottom. I tried bringing in my own K-cups once, the vanilla caramel kind, because they smell so good when they brew. But someone stole the whole box right out of my locker. You really can't trust anyone there. My husband told me I should just buy a padlock, but those combination locks are so annoying. I can never remember the three numbers. Left, right, left... or is it right, left, right? I used to have this bike lock when I was a kid, it was bright pink and it just used a little silver key. I kept the key on a shoelace around my neck. It was one of those sparkly shoelaces, you know, with the metallic threads woven into it? I loved those. I wish they still made fun shoelaces like that for adults. Everything is just boring black and brown now.
If I told you that I checked with your warehouse and they said they haven't been changing your pallet counts or watching you, what would you think about that?

I'd think they were lying to you, obviously. I mean, of course they're gonna tell you that. They're not gonna just admit to some doctor that they're sabotaging me. That's exactly why I came in here, because my husband and those warehouse people keep acting like I'm the crazy one. But I know for a fact they've been watching my moves and messing with the pallet counts so I don't get the supervisor spot. 

It's just like when human resources says complaints are "anonymous." They always say that, but everyone knows Brenda in HR talks. She sits right at the front desk with that big bowl of peppermints. They're the soft kind, the ones that melt in your mouth, not the hard little discs that crack your teeth. I cracked a molar once on a hard candy. A Jolly Rancher. The green apple ones are the best, but they are like glue on your teeth. I had to go to this emergency dentist on a Sunday, and he smelled strongly of garlic. Like, really strong, like he just ate a whole garlic bread before looking in my mouth. It was awful. I love garlic bread, though, especially with that really thick, gooey cheese on top. You have to broil it for just a minute at the end so the cheese gets those little brown bubbles. If you don't broil it, it's just soggy bread. But yeah, if you called them, they're just lying to cover their tracks. They want me to look crazy so they can give the job to someone else.

You've told me about the coworkers changing your pallet counts and watching you at work, and about your husband not supporting your supervisor promotion. Do you believe your husband is actually working together with the warehouse people to sabotage you, or do you think he's just unsupportive for separate reasons about the hours?

Look, I know I keep saying this, but it's literally the whole reason I'm sitting in this chair right now. My husband and the warehouse people are all in on it together, acting like I'm the one who's crazy. But I know for an absolute fact they are all watching my moves and changing those pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. He says it's about the hours, but he just knows they're doing it and he's going along with them. 

He works over at the auto parts store, the one with the big green sign, and he works crazy hours anyway. They make him wear these awful polo shirts. They're supposed to be forest green, but after you wash them a few times they turn into this gross, faded swamp color. I keep telling him he needs to wash them in cold water with that dark clothes detergent, like Woolite. But Woolite is so expensive now. I went to Target last week to get laundry soap and a tiny bottle was almost twenty bucks. Target is getting completely ridiculous with their prices. I used to love going there just to walk around that little dollar section right at the front when you walk in, but it's not even a dollar anymore. Everything is like three or five dollars now. I bought this little ceramic pumpkin there for Halloween last year, and it chipped on the bottom the second I set it down. I just put it on the TV stand anyway so you can't see the broken part. We have this huge flat screen he bought for the Super Bowl two years ago, it takes up the whole wall... wait, what were you asking me about my husband?

Nicole, I hear that you're absolutely certain about what's happening at work. But let me ask you this: is there any part of you, even a small part, that wonders whether these things might not actually be happening the way you believe they are?

No. No, there isn't. I mean, I know I've said it like five times now, and I only came in here because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy, but I know for a fact they have been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. I know what I see. 

It's just like when people say they didn't eat the last donut in the breakroom, but you can literally see the powdered sugar on their black pants. Powdered sugar is the worst for that. It gets everywhere. I made these powdered sugar snowball cookies for Christmas last year, the ones with the pecans inside? You have to roll them in the sugar while they're still warm so it sticks, but then you roll them again when they cool down so they get that thick white coating. My grandma used to make them, but she called them Mexican Wedding Cookies. I don't know why, she wasn't Mexican, she was from Ohio. Cleveland, I think? Or maybe Cincinnati. Cincinnati has that weird chili they serve over spaghetti. I tried it once at a diner off the interstate when we drove out there for my cousin's wedding. They put a mountain of shredded cheddar cheese on top of it. It's so strange to put chili on spaghetti, but it was actually pretty good. My cousin wore this huge puffy dress that looked like a cupcake, and her veil kept getting caught on the chairs during the reception... but no, I don't wonder if I'm wrong. I'm not wrong.

Nicole, when your husband and the warehouse people tell you that they're not watching you or changing your numbers, do you think there's any chance they might actually be telling the truth, or are you completely certain they're lying?

I am completely certain they're lying. I mean, I know I sound like a broken record today, but I literally only came in here because my husband and the warehouse guys keep acting like I'm the crazy one. But I know what's real. They are watching my every move and changing those pallet counts just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

It's like a bad soap opera, honestly. My mom used to watch General Hospital every single day at 2 PM. She would record it on VHS if she had to work. Remember those big clunky black tapes with the little plastic flap on the front that you could push open? I actually got my finger stuck in one of those flaps when I was like, seven years old. It pinched so bad I cried for an hour. My mom had to give me a cherry popsicle just to get me to stop screaming. I hate cherry flavor now, though. It tastes exactly like cough syrup. Like that red Robitussin stuff. That stuff is so nasty, but it really does work when you have that deep chest congestion that just rattles when you breathe. My husband had a cough like that last winter and it kept me up all night long. He snores too, which is just... ugh, it's unbearable sometimes. He really needs one of those CPAP machines, but he refuses to go to a sleep clinic because he hates doctors. Which is pretty rich, considering he's the one who wanted me to come see you in the first place.

Besides the situation at work with the pallet counts and the supervisor position, are there other situations in your life where you believe people are deliberately trying to harm you, sabotage you, or work against you?

No, not really. It's just the warehouse thing. Honestly, I'm only even talking to you because my husband and the guys at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. They act like I'm making it all up, but I know for a fact they've been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. It's so frustrating when people treat you like you don't know what you're seeing with your own two eyes. 

Like when my sister tries to tell me she didn't borrow my favorite denim jacket. I know she did because she left a receipt from Starbucks in the pocket. She always gets those ridiculous Frappuccinos with extra caramel drizzle. Caramel is so sticky, I don't know how she drinks that every morning. I prefer just black coffee, maybe a little splash of half-and-half if I'm feeling fancy. We used to have this diner near our old apartment that had the best coffee. The mugs were so thick and heavy, like you could drop one on the floor and it wouldn't even chip. They had these vinyl booths that were duct-taped together because the red material was splitting. It gave the place character, you know? The waitress there, Barb, she always called everyone 'hon' and she wore this bright blue eyeshadow that went all the way up to her eyebrows. You don't see people wearing makeup like that anymore. Now everyone watches those YouTube tutorials and tries to make their faces look perfectly contoured, like they're a Kardashian or something. I tried contouring once and I just looked like my face was dirty. I had to wash it all off with a washcloth, and it stained my favorite white towel... but yeah, to answer your question, it's just the stuff at work with the supervisor spot. No one else is after me.
